title: Kernel Springboard: bridge puzzles weekly
content:
Quick weekly capture – kitchen-scrap notes, hypotheses, and action items from the kernel springboard session and the related standups (tiling/prefill/bridge work). Rough — meant for the team to skim and add if I missed anything.

Context and framing:
- Week focus: reduce tail latency and reclaim batching while rolling out tile-affinity shims and the prefill-bridge change.
- Hypothesis driving this sprint: the bridge handshake between kernel A (tiler/v0) and kernel B (prefill/kv-v2) is splitting request cohorts and causing micro-batch starvation for mid-length sequences (seq_len ~512).
- Primary signals we are watching: per-kernel queue depth, p50/p95/p99 gen latency (token-level and request-level), KV cache hit-rate for warm prefixes, and GPU SM utilization.

Standup highlights (short bullets):
- Marcus: added bridge backpressure flag (bridge_backoff_ms) defaulting to 8ms; initial dogfood decreased 99p by ~12% on a synthetic midload. Observed CPU spin increase on host when backoff enabled.
- Diego: KV shadow warmup experiment (shadow warmup v3) shows faster population for reused prompts; positive for long-running sessions but introduces transient eviction bursts under contention.
- Rachel: cohort sampler change landed on canary for dedicated pool; splitting microbatches improved throughput but increased small-request jitter. Collecting per-client variance to tune sampler thresholds.
- Oliver: kernel scheduling tweak (tiling affinity bias) reduced cross-CPU migrations; still seeing leftover handshake events that kill coalescing opportunities.

What we observed this week (detailed):
1) Bridge handshake timing mismatch
- Problem: when a request arrives that needs both tiling and prefill, the order and timeout between kernel A's completion and kernel B's readiness sometimes exceeds our batching window. This breaks continuous batching and leads to many small, high-latency microbatches.
- Evidence: trace snippets show sequences where token generation waits on a prefill completion that arrives 9–12ms after tiler completion; our batching coalesce window is 10ms. These traces correlate with p99 spikes.
- Interim mitigations tested: bridge_backoff_ms, aggressive affinity pinning, and holding tiler tokens for up to 4ms hoping prefill arrives. Each reduces p99 in different slices but has tradeoffs (CPU usage, increased median latency).

2) KV cache shadow warmup behavior
- Shadow warmup v3 uses a two-phase insert: fast lightweight touch + deferred full insert. Under moderate contention the deferred queue grows and then drains in spikes, causing eviction churn.
- Impact: KV hit-rate improves for long sessions but hop-jamming causes short-lived eviction-driven misses for other cohorts. We flagged this in metrics: short-session hit-rate drops by ~2.7% during drain windows.
- Proposed tweak: introduce soft-credits limiting deferred inserts per-core and add jitter to drain schedule to avoid synchronized drains. Diego to prototype.

3) Cohort sampler and microbatch split policy
- The new sampler splits requests by arrival pattern rather than client-id for some ephemeral flows. This recovered throughput but increased jitter for small, latency-sensitive clients.
- We need a hybrid rule: prefer client-affinity for <64-token requests, arrival-cohort for >64 tokens. Rachel to open RFC and small canary.

4) Thermal/CPU observations from the dogfood run
- Bridge_backoff reduced p99 but raised host CPU sys time by ~9% on dogfood cluster. Likely busy-waiting or tighter timers. Need to profile where waiting happens (kernel thread vs poll loop). Marcus to attach perf traces.

5) New anomaly: "ghost prefill"
- Occasionally we see a prefill that claims it completed but its KV entries are missing on subsequent reads for a few ms; suspects: race between deferred insert and eviction, or NVRAM buffer reorder. Diego to dig into ordering and retry semantics.

Decisions made in the sync:
- Keep bridge_backoff_ms feature-flagged; default ON in canary, OFF in production until performance cost reduced.
- Roll forward cohort sampler but revert split policy for small latency-sensitive tenants—apply hybrid rule after the RFC.
- Prototype soft-credit drain gating for shadow warmup v3 rather than rolling back.

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Marcus: run perf traces on dogfood with bridge_backoff enabled and report hotspots (ETA: 2026-06-21). Ticket: JIRA-INF-2361.
- Diego: prototype deferred-insert soft-credit gate + jittered drain; unit test for eviction-backpressure (ETA: 2026-06-25). Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821 (WIP).
- Rachel: write RFC for hybrid cohort sampler (client-affinity threshold + arrival-based fallback); include canary plan (ETA: 2026-06-22).
- Oliver: trace the handshake path between tiler and prefill kernels; produce a micro-benchmark that reproduces the 9–12ms gap (ETA: 2026-06-20).
- All: collect per-tenant latency distribution for last 7 days and annotate any correlation with tenant config (quantization settings, pinned kernels) (ETA: 2026-06-23).

Notes to self / ideas to explore (brain dump):
- Consider handshake coalescing: if tiler finishes and prefill not ready, advertise a short coalesce window at the tiler level rather than waiting for central scheduler. This keeps coalescing logic local and reduces cross-kernel chatter.
- Evaluate a soft-reservation token for cohorts: reserve a microbatch slot for X ms for in-progress handshakes. Cost tradeoff: wasted slot vs preserved batch.
- Re-check kernel scheduling affinity when quantized kernels (int8) are mixed with float16 kernels; there might be cache line misses when switching codepaths.

Logs / snippets (copied traces):
- TRACE EXCERPT 1: request_id=abc123 -> tiler_end=12:03:14.122 -> prefill_ready=12:03:14.134 -> gen_start=12:03:14.134 -> p99 spike.
- TRACE EXCERPT 2: request_id=def456 -> deferred_insert_enqueue=12:06:18.900 -> deferred_insert_drain_start=12:06:19.120 -> eviction_burst observed 12:06:19.121..19.125.

Open questions for next sync:
- Can we reduce bridge_backoff cost by switching to event-driven wakeups instead of timers? (Marcus)
- Is deferred insert order strongly coupled to eviction codepath, or can we make deferred queue honor eviction locks to prevent transient misses? (Diego)
- Should the cohort sampler be tenant-configurable while we iterate on thresholds? (Rachel)

Appendix: quick metric snapshots (dogfood cluster, 2026-06-17):
- p50 gen latency: 18.6ms
- p95 gen latency: 63.2ms
- p99 gen latency: 185.9ms (down from 210ms with bridge_backoff)
- KV overall hit-rate: 82.1%
- Short-session (<30s) KV hit-rate during deferred drain windows: 79.4%
- Average microbatch size: 6.1 tokens/request

If you have additions or corrections, drop them inline. Planning a quick sync on Monday to triage perf traces and pick one mitigation to dogfood cluster-wide.

-- Aisha
